PRENATAL GENETIC TESTING REPORT
[redacted location] Medical Center
Department of Clinical Genetics

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Medical Record Number: [redacted ID]
Maternal Age: 20 years
Gestational Age at Sampling: 17 weeks

SPECIMEN INFORMATION
Specimen Type: Amniotic fluid
Specimen ID: [redacted ID]
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Prenatal testing for common trisomy conditions

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Fluorescence Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR) for rapid aneuploidy detection

RESULT SUMMARY
No evidence of trisomy 13, 18, or 21 detected

DETAILED RESULTS

Chromosome 13 Analysis:
Markers tested: D13S631, D13S258, D13S742, D13S628
Result: Normal diallelic pattern observed for all informative markers
Interpretation: Consistent with normal chromosome 13 complement

Chromosome 18 Analysis:
Markers tested: D18S391, D18S390, D18S535, D18S386
Result: Normal diallelic pattern observed for all informative markers
Interpretation: Consistent with normal chromosome 18 complement

Chromosome 21 Analysis:
Markers tested: D21S1411, D21S1412, D21S1435, D21S1446
Result: Normal diallelic pattern observed for all informative markers
Interpretation: Consistent with normal chromosome 21 complement

METHODOLOGY
QF-PCR analysis was performed on uncultured amniocytes extracted from 2ml of amniotic fluid. DNA was extracted using standard protocols and amplified using fluorescently labeled primers specific for polymorphic short tandem repeat (STR) markers on chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. PCR products were analyzed by capillary electrophoresis. Peak area ratios were calculated for all informative markers. Normal diallelic patterns show peak ratios between 0.8-1.4, while trisomic patterns typically show triallelic patterns or skewed diallelic ratios.

LIMITATIONS
This test screens only for trisomy of chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. Other chromosomal abnormalities, including structural rearrangements, mosaicism below 20%, and abnormalities of other chromosomes, would not be detected by this method.

FOLLOW-UP TESTING
Full karyotype analysis using G-banded chromosomes from cultured amniocytes is currently in progress and will be reported separately. This comprehensive cytogenetic analysis will evaluate all chromosomes for numerical and structural abnormalities.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Await results of full karyotype analysis for comprehensive chromosomal evaluation
2. Genetic counseling is recommended to discuss results and any further testing options
3. Continue routine prenatal care and ultrasound monitoring

This test was developed and validated by [redacted location] Medical Center Clinical Genetics Laboratory.
